title: R1. The closed system box is the control panel
problem: Decision 1 says the control panel is the diagram with everything folded away, and SPEC §4 and the image-squeeze README promise that each closed box shows its measures with value, setpoint, health and trend. What is drawn is a name, 'N feedback loops inside' and, at best, port names with bare numbers. On the-job the first screen is two empty boxes; on big, seven identical ones while goals are off. In Blocks a closed system is 'Q_service 3×3' and nothing else. So health is read from a side list and a separate Loops page, which is the 'more panels' pattern the owner wants gone. Story B1 failed outright (possible: no), as did H1; all eight designers raised it, and after briefing each said it was worse than they first thought.
proposal: Each closed system box carries, in this order: its name and description; one row per goal it holds (the goal's measure, its value, its bound, a trend over the header's window, a status word, and where it is heading); then its other exposed stocks and flows as today. Off goals come first; a box with an off goal has a heavier outline and 'N off' in its title row. The rows are the box's exposed parts, so nothing new is added to the page; a click on a row opens the evidence that exists. In Dynamics the row is the goal-seeking structure in miniature (level, desired level, gap). In Blocks the same block keeps its symbol and prints r and y on its ports with the status in text under it ('3 control loops, 1 off'), monochrome. At phone width the boxes stack one per row and become the home view, so '/' no longer needs to redirect to Loops. Once this lands, decide whether the Loops page still earns its place (its columns are now on the boxes); until then it stays.

title: R2. The system comes first; ergostat's own upkeep is set apart
problem: Every demo models ergostat's upkeep of its own model as a system, 'modelling'. That is intended. But it is drawn first (top left), its two goals lead the attention list in all six demos, they are permanently off (requests-handled 94 to 100% of the time), and on the-job and software-factory they are the whole of the red '2 loops off'. On big, 24 of 26 attention entries are its requests. It also stops the-job's only system from opening. All sixteen reviews name this; the newcomer's conclusion was 'the tool is broken, or is about itself'. Its names carry no system, against decision 5.
proposal: Keep modelling as a system, and treat it everywhere as the model's upkeep, not the subject: drawn last and dashed with a one-line label; counted apart in the header ('0 goals off · model upkeep 2'); listed after the system's own goals, under its own rule, with its requests folded; ignored by the 'alone at its level starts open' rule; collapsed at the foot of Loops. Names in every list carry their system. Then make it hold in the demos: a fixer that runs every minute and moves nothing is a dead actuator, and the first lesson every demo teaches should not be that ergostat's own feedback fails.
looks: Top level of software-factory: product and factory fill the canvas with their signed links; bottom right, a smaller dashed box 'modelling · ergostat's upkeep of this model, not the system · 2 off'. Header: '0 goals off · model upkeep 2'. Side list: 'Goals off 0', then under a thin rule 'Model upkeep: 2 off · 24 requests alike'.

title: R3. Needs attention becomes the Inbox
problem: Decision 7 makes approving or denying the one thing people do, in 'the Inbox'. There is no Inbox. Requests are rows in a side list on one page, mixed with alarms and model notes, capped at about six rows, re-sorted every few seconds, and absent from the first screen on a phone. Rows are machine text cut off with '…', point to a command line, have inputs truncated to 'how ma' and 'why (to de', put Deny before its reason in tab order, and never confirm what was done. A typed reason was lost when its row vanished. On big 24 identical requests fill the list. Story E3 and E4 failed; E1, E2 and E5 were at best partly possible.
proposal: Keep the side list where it is and make it the Inbox, in three fixed groups: Waiting for you, Goals off, Model housekeeping. A request is one sentence in plain words (what will happen, to what, who asks, why), with the command behind a disclosure, a labelled reason, and Approve and Deny of equal weight named for what they answer. The list holds still while the pointer or focus is in it; an answered row says what was done and by whom and links to the item, whose history shows it. Requests alike fold into one row with a count and one answer. A 'N wait for you' link in the header reaches the group from every page and is first on a phone. No new page: the count in the header, the group in the side list and the item pages carry all of it.

title: R4. Blocks reads as a textbook block diagram at every level
problem: At the leaf the notation is right: summing junctions, r/e/u/y/d, H on the return, relay and dead-band glyphs, C(z) with sampler and hold. Above the leaf it is not a block diagram. The top level is opaque 'Q' boxes: seven in a column with no signals on big, two unconnected on the-job, one unlabelled wire on ticket-factory; no reference, no summing junction, nothing marked off. Q is undefined and reads to a control engineer as the Youla parameter; it changes to P with different dimensions when opened. Inside, many blocks hold an agent's name and no function; loops are interleaved rather than one per row; a chain runs bottom-up; a ceiling is drawn as 'r = 0'; text is 7 to 9 px and Fit goes to 4 px. Stories G5 and G6 were only partly possible.
proposal: Draw the hierarchy with the same grammar as the leaf. At the top level each system is classified by what it holds: a controller subsystem (C), a plant-only subsystem (P, the same letter and dimensions when opened), or a named subsystem block when mixed. References enter through a summing junction; signals between systems are labelled (u_deployed); the fed-back output returns through H. Systems that share no signal are drawn as parallel rows, each with its own r and y, under the note 'no signals between these'. Inside, one loop per row, left to right, upstream first, with couplings between rows drawn downwards; every block carries its function with the agent as a caption; a one-sided limit is a limit; sensors polled alike look alike; crossings hop and only real take-offs get a dot. Status is carried without colour: an off loop's e is printed bold with its value and the word 'off'. Text never goes below 11 px: when the rows do not fit, show the rows that do and say which way the rest lies.

title: R5. Dynamics tells the system's story: goals drawn, a handful of named loops, doubt on the part
problem: The leaf notation is Sterman's and should stay. But on software-factory's product, the demo's subject, none of its three goals is drawn (image-squeeze and big do draw 'desired' and 'gap'); all 18 elementary loops are drawn with path names ('all-live via regressions and churn and asks'), their markers and names piled on each other and on the users stock; loops are called R or B while most of their links show no sign; '+1' on a marker is unexplained; polarity signs at the top level cannot be matched to their links; nothing on any part says where the model is doubtful, though the page already holds hidden rings for it. Stories G3, G4 and C6 failed.
proposal: Four changes, all inside the stock-and-flow diagram. (1) Every goal is drawn as goal-seeking structure in the system that owns it: desired level, gap, signed links. When its controller is in another system the gap's link leaves through a port ('→ factory'); when nothing serves it the gap has no outgoing link and a small 'no feedback' mark, which is the finding drawn the SD way. (2) Draw the loops that matter: those the model names, plus the shortest loop through each goal's gap; fold the rest into the side list ('13 minor loops'). A loop may carry a mechanism name in the model ('quality erosion'), written by whoever maintains the model through the Supervisor; its path stays in its panel. (3) A loop is R or B only when every link is signed; signs that hold by definition are filled in. (4) Markers sit inside the loop they name; markers, names and signs are obstacles in layout and never cover a part, a pipe or each other. Status and doubt are drawn on the part: an off goal's gap in the one accent colour with the word 'off'; a dashed stock with its unexplained change; a hatched valve on a flow whose equation fits worse than its mean; '?' on an unidentified process. At 'Everything' this gives the overview an SD study opens with: sectors, their goals, and the named loops between them.

title: R6. 'Off' tells the truth: on track, falling behind, flapping, and what to expect
problem: A goal approaching its bound on schedule (users climbing steadily to 180) is red and 'off 100%' exactly like a failing one; a queue goal goes red each time one item waits (29 times in 33 minutes); a goal that crossed its bound 23 times reads 'holding'. The headline moves between 2 and 6 within a minute on some demos. The forecast, the thing that makes this a dynamics tool, is two clicks down, takes about 20 s, looks 4 to 8 minutes ahead whatever the window, and reads 'off at +8m15s with p≈0.07 (100 runs)', which leads with 'off' for a goal 93% likely to hold. Stories B3 failed; B2 and B4 partly.
proposal: Give a goal's state the words a person would use, and say where it is heading wherever the goal is shown. States: holding; approaching (not at its bound yet, closing at a rate that reaches it within the horizon) in neutral ink; off; flapping (with its crossing count). A queue goal says in words whether one waiting item is within its tolerance or grace time. The headline counts goals off for longer than their grace, with hysteresis, and agrees with the switcher, the side list and Loops at the same moment. The forecast becomes one sentence the right way round ('likely to keep holding for the next 8 minutes, about 9 in 10', 'reaches 180 in about 6 minutes', 'will stay off'), with the horizon stated and tied to the window, and the method behind a disclosure. It is computed with the page, not on demand, and shown in the Loops row and on the box row (R1).

title: R7. The evidence for a goal is a runbook, and it agrees with the Record and Agents
problem: The evidence panel is the best thing in the product (y with r, u and e on one time axis, crossings, decisions) and every reviewer said to keep it. But the route to it is broken (goal names that look like links do nothing; opening it marks nothing on the diagram), its statements about the actor contradict the Record and the Agents page on the same screen ('never opened' beside 'Moves 1.62/h' beside 34 runs), and it answers an SRE's questions in a modeller's order and words ('Not worked out: it has no one process'). It has no link to the person's waiting ask, the items held, or the events behind it. Stories C3, C4 and C5 failed; C1 and C2 partly.
proposal: Keep the panel and its charts. Put four lines above them, built from the same counts the Record and Agents use: who or what acts and what it did ('fixer: commanded 34 times, ran 34, moved nothing; its log: no open request the rule tier answers'); what it waits on (a link to the person's ask, or the items it holds); how long it has been off against how long it usually takes; one suggested remedy with its numbers. Every mention of a goal anywhere opens this panel and rings the part. Every crossing links to the Record narrowed to this goal and time, with real timestamps and repeated events folded. The panel, the selection and the window live in the address.

proposal: One rule for every change of view: frame what the reader just asked for, at a text size they can read, and say where the rest is. After Open or Into the opened system is in view; Fit includes every node, wire and label; text never goes below 11 px (the diagram pans instead, with hints that name a direction and move there when clicked); the previous drawing stays, dimmed, until the next is ready. title: R9. The diagram can be read without a mouse or sight
problem: The owner's decision is that the diagram is the interface. Today the diagram is one unnamed SVG that Tab skips: nothing in it can take focus, so a keyboard or screen-reader user cannot open a system, select a stock, or read a block's definition, and the Loops and Agents rows that would be the text twin are mouse-only too. View and page state are not announced. Story H5 failed. As long as this holds, those users need exactly the extra pages the owner wants to remove.
proposal: Make the diagram itself the accessible structure, with no added view. First make every clickable part focusable with a name and Enter (quick fix). Then give each diagram one tab stop and let arrow keys follow the lines its discipline reads along: in Dynamics, Right and Left along the pipe, Up and Down along connectors (announcing polarity), L through the loops a part is in; in Blocks, Right and Left along the signal from r to y, Down into the feedback path. Each part announces what a sighted expert reads: 'Stock bytes-per-mp, 52.8 KB per MP, desired ≤ 20, 32.8 over, off. In loops B2 and B36.' The side panel's loop rows are the entry points. The MathML definitions already there are spoken as they are.

title: R10. Take the model out: export what lies behind the picture
problem: WHY.md leads with design documents, proposals and projection. Export offers SVG, Design SVG and PNG; the PNG is defective, and nothing exports the model. An SD modeller cannot audit the equations in one pass; a control engineer cannot take P(s), C(z) and the traces to another tool. Both experts called it the biggest missed chance for their audience. title: R11. One word for each thing: goal, feedback loop, control loop
problem: 'Loop' names two objects: an R or B feedback loop (49 of them on ticket-factory) and a goal with its control path (16, with setpoints, 'off' and 'holding'). Both sit in one panel under the same word, the header says 'N loops off', and the counts cannot be reconciled. The same goal is 'desired = 0: excess 37', 'setpoint ≤ 0 (off by 36)' and 'error −36' on three surfaces, and the Dynamics wording is produced by a find-and-replace that corrupts identifiers. The per-view vocabulary is right and should stay; its edges are what fail. Story G1 was only partly possible.
proposal: Use 'goal' for what is wanted and whether it holds: the header ('2 goals off'), the side list, the box rows and the page that lists them. Use 'feedback loop' only for R and B in Dynamics, and 'control loop' in Blocks. Where a feedback loop closes a goal, say so on both ('B40 serves goal model-fits'). Outside Blocks, say how far off in plain words with the bound as a bound ('37 over its limit of ≤ 0', '21 short of ≥ 30'); keep e = r − y with its sign in Blocks and the scope. This changes docs/vocabulary.md, where 'Loop (holding, off)' is listed on purpose, so it is the owner's decision; the recommendation is to make it, because every one of the eight reviewers tripped on it and the stories already speak of goals.

title: R12. Fewer pages, and demos that show the claims
problem: Two things stand behind the three doubts (is it useful, will people use it, will it matter) that no page change answers. First, eight top-level pages do not fit a phone or 200% zoom, and three of them (Loops, Agents, Model) are tables of the same goals again, while Check is a lint list for whoever maintains the model. Second, the demos do not show what WHY.md argues: no loop in six demos has an identified process, so margins, closed-loop step, Bode and tuning never appear; no demo has an observed external controller ('fixing the controls we already pay for'); every demo's own upkeep is off; ticket-factory leaves nothing to approve.
proposal: Pages: fold Check into Model as its 'Findings' section (both answer 'is the model right?'), which leaves seven; revisit Loops after R1 and Agents after R4 (an agent is a block; its runs and cost fit that block's panel). Decide each by use, not now. Demos: one whose loop has an identified process with its step test already run; one with an observed external controller (the kube-sim autoscaler is the candidate) identified as C(s) with its saturation and lag and a proposed retune; a healthy start where modelling holds; a few outward actions left waiting.
